txt: He blinks, waiting for the next question.
He considers this for a moment. "Yeah, that interpretation holds."
He cringes. "Weird stuff. Specialized. There was a data processor and some sort of long-wave machinery."
He gives you a long, suspicious look. "Correct."
He is shifting in his spot uncomfortably, still feeling sorry for the mishap.
He nods: "What's on your mind?"
He picks up a wrench and scratches his head with it, unaroused by fascism.
He shakes his head. "I don't say much anything as a carpenter anymore. They tried to make me into a reckoner and a leveller. Made me a bit manic, y'know?"
He shrugs, as though the point were rather obvious.
He shrugs. "I don't know. Maybe. Maybe not. It's not a thing we can answer, cop-man. Even I have limits -- I'm a limited-psy person."
He shrugs. "It's your transmission. A regular old transceiver should work fine, it just won't be as *hard core*, you know..."
He shrugs. "They're hard core."
He thinks. "Or maybe he's not dead, maybe he's just really ecstatic about the beats."
He throws a screwdriver and a bunch of drill chucks into the corner and explodes into dance. What he lacks in sharpness, he more than makes up for in violent enthusiasm.
His chest returns to its normal proportions. "I'm sorry."
His eyes flicker.
His friend hands you his papers. The name reads: 'Karl Holtzmann.'
His look is intensely suspicious.
In the background, his friend drops a heavy electric drill. He, too, waits for your judgement with undivided attention.
It's a bit hypnotizing if you look at it long enough.
Just like that the speedfreak is right in your face, his eyes burning. His comrades look on worriedly.
Noid shakes to the beat. There are no tools in his hands at the moment. He appears to ignore you.
Noid straightens his back, ready for the beat...
Noid surveys the situation with his face pale and blank. His eyebrow is twitching.
Noid watches you pick up the key with a smirk.
The church creaks in response. The speedfreak is too busy listening to it with a suspicious expression to say anything.
The contents of the young man's toolbox are organized in a neat, yet eclectic manner. He is constantly checking out the various tools and parts and rearranging them slightly...
The skinny wraith looks at you with some disbelief.
The speedfreak eyes you with a curious blend of awe and contempt.
The speedfreak looks the same way. It is dark there, in the back of the church. For a moment the music echoes strangely.
The speedfreak nods to you.
The speedfreak's eyes narrow with suspicion, as if he's looking at a man possessed.
The young man doesn't move. His earrings rattle from the tension. With his jaw clenched, he says:
The young man doesn't say anything either. After a while he takes out a magnet and runs it over some nails in front of him.
The young man gives you an uncharacteristic smile as you're turning to leave.
The young man looks startled.
The young man looks straight up, following the line of your finger. A frown comes over his face.
The young man picks up a level and inspects it against the floodlight. The water sparkles in the small measuring tube. "Yes," he says after a while. "I think it's correct to say that."
The young man picks up a thin metal saw blade and nods.
The young man rubs his chin, in silence, then mumbles: "... like a concentric ring spreading out... the struggling villages..."
The young man shrugs. "I doubt it. I don't even think the Ubis properly understood it. What it does. But it's what this Soona person is looking for, and trying to measure." He nods toward the woman.
The young man smiles and nods. Slowly he picks up two hammers at once.
The young man with earrings looks at you suspiciously.
The young man with ribcage-shaped suspenders looks at you standing there -- with a goofy grin on your face.
The young speedfreak gives you a suspicious look before returning to... whatever he was doing.
The young speedfreak puts down a busted capacitor and looks at you.
Without a word the other speedfreak pulls a red wallet out of the toolbox and hands it to you.
"'I saw some piglets suckling their dead mother' -- have you heard this one, cop-man?" He continues without waiting for an answer: "'After a short while they shuddered and went away.'"
"*And* short. *And* memorable!"
"*Anodic* dance music," he nods. "Regular dance music wasn't hard enough. And yes, I do."
"*I* only said: *Unity*. One word. Figures of authority always misquote you." He points to his friends.
"*Mental illness* is a term the powers use to homogenize people. I think I don't reach mental illness. I am merely politically ill. A suspicious element."
"*No one* says Arno van Eyck is a mass murderer. The anodic pioneer Rietveldt is not a mass murderer. He is not accused of mass murder..."

"*Total*. Everything between an ancient concrete cathedral and a glass cube is Dolorianism. This is just a homespun version of it, folksy stuff, early mass production. They made thousands like this. Does that help you out?"
"... and that is what caused the communards to fail in defending the beachhead. Yeah, a lot of failure has gone down around here."
"A Seraise man, who lived a long time ago. An ancient hard core brother."
"A cop who's into building critique." He taps a floorboard. "Okay then. This is folk Dolorianism, lawmongerer. It's a subset of early *Dolorian* architecture."
"A cop-on-cop challenge, not bad. Let's see what you come up with... Though I have to say, cop cars and lorries usually pack the best equipment in town."
"A dead guy smiling."
"A life is true if it's free from fear and internal division among oneself. And others -- mankind has seeds of greatness in it. A germinal will come, a return to trueness. It will be hard core."
"A reasonable question. Say, I get hurt. I want to make sure it never happens again. So I analyse the situation. Exercise caution. Caution is suspicion."
"A sticker... you mean the yellow one? Can you describe it to me?"
"A three-thousand-year-old tyrannical regime of History, built and maintained by hundreds of generations of self-appointed *intellectuals*..." He looks around. "It's false-core."
"About time. You grab that amp. Forget the cables. Need to leave some evidence of our antenna to inspire future generations..."
"Again."
"All I have to do is run a cable from the engine up the centaur-man's memorial. It won't last forever, but it should buy us enough time to get you synced up with the Big Bad."
"All large human gatherings are narcotic. Ask any such undertaking in history -- this included." He nods toward a human-shaped pillar nearby. "Chemistry is true to its word."
"Alone on an uninhabited archipelago, forced to face themselves and nature. Pre-industrial quantities of solitude. The sea. Perhaps something more... fundamental."
"Alright, cop-man. We've held up more than our share of this collaboration. I hope you *recognise* how much the hardcore underground came through for you."

"Alright, lawfarer, we're ready to do this. I have to warn you, though, once we commit, there's no stopping until we've seen it *all the way through*. No pauses, no second-chances. This is our shot. You got it?"
"Alright." The speedfreak dips into his belt pack and produces a yellow key. He then makes a sudden, cool-infused move, tossing it in your general direction.
"Also, they don't heat or clean the building. Shit's gonna collapse."
"An audio shortfall, you say?" The other speedfreak points his thumb toward the speaker in the back. "Guess what, we've got speakers with *massive* low end. There's a good chance it can do it."
"An ordinary white-collar transceiver joins the hard core underground. Yeah, this should do nicely..."
"And if it *can't*, well..." He shrugs non-committally.
"And of all cellular-based life. What's your point, law-bringer?"
"Andre doesn't care about the Ecclesiastes. He just wants the operation to run smoothly. And Egg is a demi-beast. You shouldn't listen to what people say, you should listen to what they are."
"Anodic music will *definitely* contain whatever we're dealing with." His words echo in the chamber...
"Anyhow, what was the sticker like?"
"Anyway, he's been giving me kind of a *psychic rundown* of this place..."
"Are they really gonna let us have this?"
"Are you a commie-cop?"
"Are you partying up there?"
"At least crab-man seems like an *advanced* being. He's hard. He'll understand."
"Bad news, lawman. Signal's going down. These waves are receding. Time to let go..."
"Bad news." The speedfreak removes his sweat-drenched headphones. "Even with the de-spooker flipped, the signal is still too weak to get down with..."

"Beats and bright lights to shatter falsehoods. Nerve impulses for the collective body. We are very much alike in basic structure. A hard enough beat would awaken everyone to a truer calling -- in unity!"
"Besides, our own sines aren't even synced yet. So how am I supposed to get *you* synced up with the Big Bad? It doesn't make any sense, law-lover."
"Between you and me -- I don't know if you've noticed this about me... I'm a little *suspicious* of authority. But you -- you really came through for the hard core underground."
"Burnouts!" He angrily spits on a screw, then starts cleaning it.
"But it's all blocked with that stupid traffic jam right now! Anyway..."
"But not really," the other one adds. "Brown hair. Old. Heavy, dark sines."
"But that's exactly what drugs are for. Exactly. Time to expand your mind!"
"But that's what everybody saw. Explain it as you please, but it doesn't really do to just deny it ever happened."
"But that's what the invalids' fund is for, so don't worry about it for now."
"But were you wrong? The Founding Party is okay with everything. Look around." He spreads his arms. "They do not have enough love for the *human crew* to oppose anything anymore. We're on our own."
"C'mon. Okay, then." He looks surprised and a bit disappointed. "You don't have to describe it. What did you want to know about the sticker?"
"Can't do it. We just got this place set up. Can't go risking Egg's most important equipment..."
"Centaur-man is made of metal. With the right gear we could make it work."
"Climb down from the equestrian monument, cop-man. Consciousness is new to the universe. We all have our ways to ease the shock."
"Come on. My leg's starting to twitch. Means we've been here too long..."
"Cool. The ban on foulness, that's the moralists' plot to alienate us from our bodily functions so they can control us more fully..."
"Could be he's your guardian spirit, your cop daemon..."
"Damn spookers. Can't keep 'em off our back..."
"Dead bodies of perennial plants." He taps on the wood. "Sigma functions have left this place. It's a good thing we came along -- the spiritual collapse has been total."
"Dead body, spirit entered. What is there to talk of?"
"Didn't know cops made that kind of lucre. This is a brilliant piece of equipment. Maybe even *too* brilliant. Feels out of step with our whole operation..."
"Didn't think so. You gotta watch out for those guys. Give off a real *hostile* sine, if you ask me."
"Do it for the masses, do it for the crew." His friend forms a fist with a screwdriver still in his hand. Approvingly so.
"Do what you have to do. We're not going anywhere."
"Don't be a lunatic. Of course he isn't. Germaine here just yells random things. Odds are, sooner or later one of them will come off as thought reading."
"Don't know how much juice we've got, so we better get to it. You ready?"
"Don't know. If we can't get around the interference, we're in deep trouble. Hold on, I think Egg gave me some kind of checklist..."

"Don't listen to him," the man yells over the music. "He's making shit up. There's no top-secret cop audio tech -- there's other top-secret-spying-on-people tech most likely, but cops don't care about *music*."
"Don't listen to that retrograde class warrior, Egg."
"Don't sweat that. Egg found something down near the waterlock. Some maniac *abandoned* a perfectly good power source..."
"Don't think so. Big Bad frequencies are extremely negative: thought suppression, dream implantation, memory revision. Pretty *out there* stuff, not sure I want to get involved with it."
"Don't worry, man. I'll remember them."
"Drugs and anodic music, I mean. And she doesn't like either one of them. Some people are just *born* retrograde."
"Dude's seen some crazy shit. But he's actually a lot like us."
"Egg Head actually has a better concept of the hard core. He just really likes saying 'hard core'."
"Egg makes a good point. An underground antenna's probably not the best way to contact your aerostatic."
"Egg means the situation is monitored." The man nods grimly. "It's 'relatively' safe. No one has died yet."
"Egg's right, they can call it 'No Truce' if it's too long. At least it stands out from the others, it *evokes* something, it's victorious."
"Either way, you gotta keep it up till we get through."

"Encasement. Confinement. Of something they were afraid of. Something new and unheard of on the isola." He looks up, into the darkness  beyond the beams. "I think that's what the crab-man is experiencing when he climbs around upstairs..."
"End of human development. Mission. Complete."
"End of quote. This is a high-quality carcass." He kicks the floorboard. "The power of anodic beats and hard bass is needed to reanimate it."
"Exactly. You could buy one, you could steal one..."
"Fame is a false existence. It doesn't happen inside the *head*." He nods mysteriously, then lets go of the suspenders and they hit his chest with a slap.
"For me it was my favourite part. Chemistry is great. Besides, imagine all the drugs we could do if we had our own drug lab."
"Fuck this. Take us in or kill us. We're not bowing any longer."
"Fuck yeah!"
"Get our fucking foot in the door."
"Give him a moment." He comes over with a cup of water and puts it to your lips. "See, this is why you need distilled water."
"Give him a moment." He comes over with a cup of water and puts it to your lips. "You've gotta drink water, man."
"Give it another go."
"Go speak to Andre. I'm just the Noid," a strangely dressed young man says without looking up from his toolbox.
"Good call, not exposing yourself to stuff like that."
"Good catch, Art Cop." He crosses his arms. "The herdsmen of the Ubi Sunt? islands came here on the first boats. Their flowery version of Dolorianism could be what we're standing in."
"Good thing you didn't squash him."
"Good, good." He likes what he's hearing. "What did you want to know?"
"Good, we have too many opinions anyway."
"Good. We're live in two... one..."
"Guess it would be pretty soft core for me to say no, wouldn't it?" He gnaws a screw thoughtfully.

"Ha!" The young man stretches his ribcage made of suspenders. "I like this question, cop-man. She did not live the life of a human. She lived like someone who is playing a game. The life of an operator..."

"Ha!" The young man stretches his ribcage made of suspenders. "I like this theory of yours, cop-man. This one I like..." He nods. "She was not human. Not really. She was an operator, playing life like a game..."
"Hang on, I'm looking at Egg's checklist. He says: 'IF ALL FAILS, BEND ANTENNA. NARROW IS THE HARD CORE WAY'... That make any sense to you?"
"Happy to help."
"Hard of core." He nods appreciatively.
"Hard to say, cop-man. Sines in here are distinctly *wild*. Gonna take a while before everything's properly *synced*..."
"Has anything like this happened to you before? Like... a *seizure*?"
"Have you been listening to what Egg's been saying? Love is *hard core* man, and a mother's love is the hardest core of all..."
"He defeated History. We are living in the age of History, and in the eyes of History we are always already dead. How can we ever smile, then? Because History is a lie, and so are its deaths..."
"He means like one of those rich-boy private radio stations, where you can listen to people getting killed on. Then jerk off to it... sick shit."
"He said it was for his nose. What more do you want?"
"He's not a communist. That's just something he likes to yell. He picked it up from a tape-jockey at The Paliseum... *she* was a communist though."
"He's right. All we're missing now is the transceiver itself. Soon as you find one, we'll be all set."
"Hell yeah." He picks up a small hammer and holds it out, ritualistically.
"Here they are."
"Here we go again!!!"
"Here, you'll like this. It's got a little straw and everything so you can slurp while you work."
"Hey, it kind of *does* look like you." He thinks for a moment. "Surely a sign of things to come. What did you want to ask about it?"
"Hey, lawman. We're waiting on you."
"Hmh. Then it's inexplicable. Whatever." He picks up his toolbox, then puts it back down again.
"Hmh." The young man nods, he looks worried. "You may be on to something, copper-man. She's got those mass murderin' hips."
"Hmm, some equipment from harbour could work. Worth the leg-work, at least."
"Hmmm. Good question. Maybe he's saying we're casting too wide a net, got to *narrow our receiving band*, so we pick up the Big Bad without the spookers."
"Hmmm. Says here, 'MAIN STEP: VOLUME TO THE MAX'... That's not too helpful. Okay, it also says: 'INSPECT CONNECTIONS FOR HARD CORE CLARITY,' so let's try that..."
"Honestly, that might be for the best. Like I said, the sines coming off this whole project are seriously uncharted..."
"How should I know? It's up to everyone to know their own needs. Whatever keeps your *body and soul* in top working condition..."
"Huh, I see you're here again, off-sine-man." He rummages through his tools. "Did I mention getting us into the church would help?"
"Huh. I don't know what to do then..."
"Huh. Sounds like Egg's saying you could use some spare cables to rig up the stalled motor lorries and increase the wavelength..."
"Huh. Sounds like that was a false move. Signal's even worse now."
"Humanism leads to eating sugar and pigs. Humanism was invented to mass produce billions of humans. Billions of humans can mass produce *hundreds* of billions of pigs."
"I *WOULD*."
"I bet he's got a shit-load of questions."
"I can see that. And you've partied *very* hard for a *very* long time, haven't you?"
"I can see that. Further sine-matching would do good for us. One way to achieve sine-synchronicity would be by getting us into the *church*."
"I did get to talk to the crab-man, though."
"I didn't know it was in here." He cracks his neck. "We have to get rid of it. Dismantle it. Can't dance with a giant *mass murderer* lookin' at you. Not a good look for the club."

"I don't have a top ten list of things I'm most suspicious of. But if I *had* one, the left-right complex would be number one. Number two would be their sole accomplishment -- the pig/wheat paradigm."
"I don't know. Buy one? Steal one? I don't know your cop ways."
"I don't trust the fat man. Gives off a hard core würm sine, real manipulative, if you ask me."
"I don't." He looks over his shoulder. "Fucker giving me the evil eye."
"I dunno... and it's not something they properly understood either. What it does. But it's what this Soona person is looking for, and trying to measure." He nods toward the woman.
"I guess it's not a *massive* problem, now that I think of it."
"I guess one could write an entire treatise on the thing. But what for?"
"I had to do it in a hurry. Not my best work... But it should hold for a while."
"I have all kinds of screws." He holds up a handful.
"I know, it's completely mental, but someone drove a *perfectly good* Coupris MC straight into the bay. Carriage is totalled, but luckily the engine on the back is still working..."
"I know, man, I was just talking about the aesthetic."
"I mean, anodic music is great and all, but drugs -- they make you feel really good. When did you last feel really, really good?"

"I prefer not to. Both ask the wrong questions. Any spark of light from either one is accidental. Their combined movement's only concern is producing enough pig and wheat for everyone -- the end goal of humanity..."
"I really am sorry, man -- just take this, okay?" He pulls out some black paper from his belt-pack.
"I regret the time I dedicated to that profession, and that worker collective. I say things more as a member of the hard core psi-dance community these days."
"I suck at socializing, man. Even now our sine synchronization is way off. But I'll see what I can do." He continues to rearrange his tools.
"I suck at socializing, man. If you go speak to Andre, I'll have time to *tune in*. Get a reading on your *sine*." Before he's finished talking, he's already turned back to his tools.
"I think it's just happenstance. Chaos in action. Contingencies of our limited existence. That and Egg Head's fantastic talent." He nods to his friend behind the turntables.

"I told you, Andre." A voice from the back of the church. "People don't want to see that woman when they're dancing. It's unhealthy. And we're *not* putting disco lights on it. That would only make it worse."
"I will, law-man." The young man nods and drops a drill chuck into a plastic container.
"I would much rather tell you about true life than this pathetic *something else*, but you are, after all, the law of the land."
"I would want to build a safe place for myself and my own as well..." His voice echoes in the wooden cavern of the church.
"I'd have a whole lot more stuff if I had a place where I could keep that stuff."
"I'll put this tech away later. Think there's an extra can set, in case you want to grab a *souvenir* or something. Don't think anyone will miss it."
"I'm doing what I can." He continues to rearrange his tools.
"I'm going to turn all the dials to maximum. Probably gonna burn out our power supply, but that might be the only way..."
"If some want to lead and others want to be led, I think they are welcome to it."
"If that's the case, though, not sure I want to get mixed up in your patron's boat business."
"In the true life of tomorrow, every woman will be an innocence. They will wear neon headbands and leggings, and they will glow in the dark." His eyes smile enigmatically.
"Is that what this switch does? I'll flip it now."
"Is that what you call those radio-spookers? Didn't know they had a *technical* name..."
"It is cool. But it's also more than that. *Much* more."
"It is, it's the time of desperate measures. He's using his party fuel to clean the connections..."
"It is."
"It looks like you're trying to hang yourself with it. So large, too. So many different patterns. It's crazy man, I like it."
"It never was. A three-thousand-year-old regime of History, built by hundreds of generations of self-appointed *intellectuals*..." He looks around. "It's false to the core."
"It says here 'MUSCLE-STYLE'."
"It should be sold," he nods, "but not by us."
"It took us setting out for this whole enterprise to get our sines synced..."
"It was stalking Acele. Exhibiting ambush behaviour."
"It wasn't quite *human* -- if you know what I mean."
"It'll be fruitless, though. She won't be able to measure it. People like that always want to measure everything, all those things they really can't."
"It's a miracle of carpentry. Dead bodies carved into *total* shapes. Now it can be something more." He rubs his hands together.
"It's a necessity. All large human gatherings are narcotic. It's just the way of the spinal cord."
"It's getting louder..." says Noid, his eyes riveted on the strange circle of water basins.
"It's gonna be the most hard core antenna in Martinaise, and probably all of Revachol West."

"It's good you talked to Andre first. Gave me time to get a reading on your *sine*. Can't really talk to people before you get a reading." He runs his hand through his hair, which is combed back in mock seriousness, and continues to fiddle with some gears.
"It's got to be you. I'm manning the decks down here."
"It's just a style, you know? Normal hard style. Anyone can wear it."
"It's just a style, you know?"
"It's like, up from here. You just go outside, and then turn up."
"It's our only shit." He shrugs. "We should make better use of not being animals -- or cereal grain -- ourselves."
"It's settled, then. Everyone, welcome to Revachol West!" He looks around the church as light beams paint the dance floor violet blue.
"It's settled, then. Everyone, welcome to THE RETURN!" He looks around the church as light beams paint the dance floor violet blue.
"It's short for *paranoid*."
"Just plug that in there, would you?"
"Just radio-spookers. We get them all the time around here. Keep trying."
"Keep trying. We'll get through these radio-spookers eventually."
"Law-man, be real careful and sensible about what you're about to do." Noid is slowly shifting his hand toward a hammer.
"Like Egg said."
"Like that Dolorian word for the world, you mean? Elysium..."

"Like that woman there," he nods toward the stained glass window. "Vertical, thin, white, a false image of grandeur. The source of the system is up there, you're at the bottom. They really dug that power vertical."
"Like, this is some old world shit the Ubis had heard about... and thought the best way to deal with it was to build a church. Surrounding it. To contain it."

"Liked to show off large and intricate structures, arches, spires. Put you down with them. They were really into painting everything white too. Virginal shit, you know. Marriage shit. Virtue and tyranny."

"Likewise, no one says Germaine Egg-Head or Andre are mass murderers. You can live *entirely* outside that suspicion. Billions of people go about not being guilty of mass murder." He nods up. "Just not her."
"Listen, no matter what happens when they get hold of you, don't you *dare* rat out the hard core underground..."
"Look at you, honour-man."
"Look, I'm not a blame-layer. I'm just saying, things were bad, and now they're worse."
"Looks like it's working. Keep going, just a bit more..."
"Man, I'm super sorry. That was totally my bad, I got overexcited. Threw them too hard. I'm sorry."

"Many non-Occidental cultures share a beat at their heart. Thus, they are closer to true, hard core life. There's just never been enough of them, and they had to rely on some extremely basic percussion."
"Maybe *you* can figure things out, cop-man. I think we got on a good level here... the sines are syncing up well."
"Maybe not that big, but pretty big."
"Maybe you break an arm, maybe you break your neck. Could go either way, honestly."
"Maybe you're being too specific about it. Try consulting with your spinal cord."
"Maybe, if you want to pay money like some kind of... money lord. Yeah, pawnshop could have one."
"Maybe." He looks up under the rafters. "Maybe they were unable to face the nature of the world -- perishing."
"Me neither. Just keep trying. We'll get through these radio-spookers eventually."
"Me too... I shouldn't have that kind of power over another person. I'm not the one with the violence monopoly here -- you are. I'm glad that key is out of my hands now."
"Most of it doesn't exist, but there's also stuff that isn't *allowed* to exist because the moralists think it's too *dangerous* for the plebes."
"My bad."
"My guess, you climb up the centaur-man, see if there's anything obviously *interfering* with them. Maybe you've got some technical law-science?"
"Na... huh. Still strongly out of sync. Stage gamma dis-alignment."
"Nah, every bit helps. We need this antenna to be as hard core as humanly possible."
"Nationalism, militarism, racism, and emphasis on a leader character are totally absent in *hard core*." The words echo through the church majestically.
"Neither will anyone else."
"New sines, new ideas, new beginning."
"No can do. This is it. The only way forward is the hard core way, straight through. Now give it another go."
"No fucking way."
"No idea what we're gonna hear when I turn this thing on, so be prepared for *anything*. Trick is to keep transmitting your request until the Big Bad acknowledges you. You got that?"
"No matter," the paranoid young man mumbles gruffly. "Is he going to be a problem?"
"No need to fake it, we know you're still a cop at heart..."
"No one can find us here."
"No telling, lawman. You ever confirmed that he's, you know, *flesh and blood*?"
"No time. We're live in two... one..."
"No use, man. Don't think he can hear you."
"No use. The Big Bad can't hear us, just the main cop."
"No way I'm getting on a boat owned by the Wild Pines. Everything about them gives off a real *shadowy* sine."
"No way. Big Bad's coming here..."
"No wonder." He cracks his neck. "We have to get rid of it. Dismantle it. Can't dance with a giant *mass murderer* lookin' at you. Not a good look for the club."
"No, but you see, no one likes *drunk* people, drunk people get into fights and try to hit on everyone. Now, people on *speed*, however..."
"No, it won't be. There can't be a first of something that can't be."

"No, it's just a vest of suspenders made to resemble a human rib cage. Plus some lady-clothes to piss off the sex-system." He points to your tie. "Now tell me about that hard core necktie. It's fucking primal."
"No, it's pretty fucking *un*-sound if you ask me. They should have built a club for anodic music around it instead." He grins...
"No, these are just boring, normal, hard core clothes. That..." he points to your necktie, "*that's* outlandish."
"No." The one with the necklace stares at you coldly. "You don't get to say one thing and then 'change your mind'. We trusted you, cop-man."
"No." The one with the necklace stares at you coldly. "You don't get to squeeze out every drop of us after keeping us in the dark for so long."
"No." The one with the necklace stares at you coldly. "You don't get to squeeze out every drop of us and then 'change your mind'."
"No." The one with the necklace stares at you coldly. "You don't get to take all our money and then 'change your mind'.
"Nope. Politics is an inert complex of daily corruption and inane thinkpieces. The real paradigm is economic and it concerns pig and wheat."
"Nope."
